title: Cross-corpus latency probe and golden-anneal workload harness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a benchmarking harness that (1) runs differential kernel selection experiments across diverse corpus slabs, (2) introduces a 'golden-anneal' baseline stabilization process to reduce noise in CI, and (3) wires deterministic perf gates into CI that trigger triage workflows when regressions exceed defined SLO thresholds.

Motivation: Current golden baselines are brittle for mixed prefill/decode workloads and we see high variance when candidate kernel swaps run against single-profile workloads. This ticket implements a suite that (a) stitches multiple corpus slabs (short-chat, long-context, code-completion, retrieval-augmented prompts) into coordinated runs, (b) samples by traffic-weighted proportions to reflect production mixes, and (c) includes an annealing schedule (progressive sequence-length scaling + sample reseeding) to converge on stable golden metrics.

Design overview:
- Multi-slab runner: orchestrates N slab workers that emit sequences to the runtime with configurable proportions and seed locking. Slabs include: short-chat (<=64 tokens), medium-dialog (128-512), long-context (1k-8k prefills), and bursty-code (short prefill, long decode).
- Differential kernel probe: for each run the harness cycles candidate kernel selection policies (baseline, ensemble-chooser-v1, latency-prioritized, cost-prioritized) and collects per-token latency, GPU utilization, kv-cache hit rates, and tail quantiles (p50/p90/p99).
- Golden-anneal stabilization: create golden runs that perform progressive sample annealing over 5 stages (seed lock, low-variance selection, mixed replay, traffic-weighted resampling, convergence checkpoint). Each stage records stability metrics and only promotes a golden snapshot when variability envelope < 3% for p95 latency and < 2% for token throughput across 10 independent seeds.
- Synthetic spike injection: intermittently injects adversarial traffic (high-concurrency bursts, long-pass-through prompts) to verify graceful degradation and fallback policies.
- CI integration: harness produces machine-readable artifacts (ndjson lines) and a summary JSON with delta metrics. CI perf gates are defined as: no >5% regression in p95 latency across golden snapshot, no >8% regression in average token cost, and no >10% regression in success/fallback rate.
- Triage flow: when CI gates fail, the pipeline auto-opens a triage issue with attached artifacts, a preliminary diff report, and a suggested rollback plan (pin to previous golden snapshot).

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can run end-to-end in the perf-cluster and produce repeatable golden snapshots in <6 hours for the 4-slab suite (on dedicated benchmark nodes).
- CI integrates the summary JSON and fails the pipeline when any gate is violated.
- A dashboard (perf/golden-anneal) shows historical golden snapshots, per-kernel breakdowns, and spike annotations.
- Runbooks updated with instructions to run the harness locally and interpret outputs.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Annealing increases runtime of golden generation but reduces CI flakiness; trade-off chosen in favor of stability to reduce costly false alarms.
- We sample traffic-weighted proportions rather than perfect mimicry of individual customer workloads; this improves generalization but may underrepresent niche patterns.
- Kernel cycling at scale increases GPU churn; mitigated by limiting parallel kernel candidates per GPU and running candidate rotations at low-traffic hours.

Artifacts and links:
- Spec / runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Cross-Corpus+Golden-Anneal+Spec
- Draft design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427
- Initial harness implementation branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/tree/feature/golden-anneal
- Perf dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.internal.redwood.ai/d/bench/golden-anneal
- Example CI artifact: gs://redwood-perf/golden-anneal/ENG-865019/2026-03-08/summary.json

QA / Validation plan:
- Smoke: run 3 short runs with fixed seeds (short-chat slab only) and verify reproducible p50/p95 within 2%.
- Stability: perform 10 independent golden-anneal runs and confirm promotion conditions are met at least 8/10 times.
- Regression simulation: intentionally flip kernel selection to a slower kernel and verify CI gates catch a p95 regression >5% and open triage issue.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): enable harness in perf-cluster with read-only CI gating for 1 week; observe false positive rate and adjust annealing schedule.
- Stage 2 (enforce): enable hard CI perf gates after 2 weeks with monitoring and a 48h rollback window.
- Stage 3 (automate): integrate auto-triage templates and a dashboard notifier to on-call.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: scoped with PM and reliability. Marco and Asha to own implementation. Decided on 4 canonical slabs to start. (Asha)

2026-03-03 - Design review: Ben (infra) flagged GPU churn; we limited kernel candidates to 3 concurrent per GPU and will run full candidate sweep during low-traffic windows. Action: update design doc to include backoff policy. (Marco)
2026-03-06 - Implementation: initial multi-slab runner committed on branch feature/golden-anneal. Basic artifacts (ndjson) emitted. PR opened: runtime#1427. (Marco)

2026-03-08 - First full golden-anneal run: produced snapshot but variance exceeded threshold on p95 (4.6%). Observed high variance driven by long-context slab; added seed-locking on prefill sampler to reduce jitter. (Asha)
2026-03-09 - CI integration: prototype CI job writes summary to GCS and posts result to perf dashboard. Work remaining: create machine-readable failure payload to auto-open triage issue. (Marco)

2026-03-10 - Decision log: We will accept a longer golden generation window (target 6h) in exchange for reduced reruns. PM approved. Next: finalize gate thresholds and create triage issue template. (PM review: Lena Ortiz)
2026-03-10 - Blockers: need a small quota bump on perf-cluster GPUs for parallel slab runs. Infra ticket opened: INF-1208. Estimated unblock in 2 business days. (Marco)
